2023 State Profile - Kansas

Child Maltreatment Victims

About this Report

This report provides data from 2023 on child maltreatment victims in Kansas. Child abuse and neglect, also referred to as child maltreatment, encompasses any recent action or failure to act by a parent or caregiver that results in significant physical or emotional harm, sexual abuse, exploitation, or death. It also includes any behavior (or lack of action) that poses an immediate risk of serious harm to a child. For more information on child maltreatment, visit the Children’s Bureau’s Child Maltreatment page from the Office of the Administration for Children and Families. The data for this report was sourced from the Kids Count Data Center.


Victims of child maltreatment

In 2023, there were 693,770 children in Kansas. During that same year, state officials reported that 1,790 children were victims of maltreatment, representing a rate of 3 per 1,000 children in the population. This report highlights the percentage of child maltreatment victims in Kansas, broken down by the following categories:

  • Gender
  • Race and Ethnicity
  • Age
  • Maltreatment Type
